chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Suwayd al-Qalla' from Abu Ayyub from Abu Basir from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who forgets and prays four rak'at during travel. He said: 'If he remembers on that day, he should repeat [the prayer]; and if he does not remember until that day passes, there is no need for him to repeat [it].'

Because what this report contains of the command to repeat after the time has passed on that day is understood as recommended (istihbab), and what the first report contains while the time is still remaining is understood as obligatory (wujub).
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a traveler who forgets to shorten his prayer and prays four rak'at?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle of *al-asl al-sihha* (presumption of validity) for travelers who mistakenly perform full prayers (*tamam*) due to forgetfulness, provided they rectify it within the same day. The juristic commentary clarifies that the command to repeat is obligatory (*wajib*) while the prayer time remains, but becomes recommended (*mustahabb*) if the day passes, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ease and the non-punitive nature of unintentional errors in travel. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia fiqh in accommodating the practical difficulties of *safar* (travel) while maintaining ritual integrity.
